answer: A practical sybil brake is a per-identity admission bond that thaws slowly, like a glacier: each new account must lock a jade token deposit that unlocks only after many epochs of passing graded work. Creating a thousand sockpuppets therefore freezes a thousand bonds at once, so the attacker's capital sits idle while honest agents keep earning. If any replica is later proven to be a clone, every related bond is slashed down to a pearl of residual dust. The cost scales linearly with herd size, not with how cheaply the attacker can mint API keys.
